posts.html:
Begin with the window

The rain made the garden look loosely drawn. At the window the branches shook, and the book on the table stayed open where I had left it. I read the same page twice because I liked where the sentence put me.

Make room for a return

The best place to read may be somewhere you can leave a book open and return to it. I keep a pencil nearby. A line in the margin tells me what I noticed last time.

At the first stall

There were pears in shallow wooden trays and green tomatoes wrapped in old newspaper. The seller could tell which pears I meant by the way I reached.

Bring the season home

I bought what smelled good and asked when it would be ripe. Back home, I wrote both answers down.

One detail at breakfast

The light crossed the table as slowly as the butter softened. I wrote that down while I could still see both changes happening together.

Keep notes close to the thing

A line about a morning can start with the glass, the floor, or the sound from the street. Concrete details give you somewhere to begin.

Past the last house

The pavement ended beside a linden tree. For a few steps the path was narrow enough that the long grass touched both ankles.

Return in another season

I plan to walk the same path when the branches are bare. A place I know in summer can still surprise me in winter.

Leave a little space

I cleared one shelf for books I have been meaning to start. I put the shortest one at eye level and opened it while the kettle boiled.

Let a first page be enough

Some evenings I only read the opening page. That is still a way of finding the book I want to spend time with next.
